speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to narrow down the cause, can you tell me exactly how long ago these symptoms started and how often you are vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jejunal Atresia

The patient is a newborn presenting with bilious vomiting, which indicates a lower GI obstruction. The absence of meconium passage and the history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis suggest a congenital intestinal anomaly rather than the more common malrotation with volvulus. To confirm the diagnosis and determine the level of obstruction, I will request an abdominal X-ray.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
